key_insight: This study maps demographic-associated information in routine pathology images at health-system scale, covering 1.3 million slides from 257,322 patients across 25 organs. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so specific findings about demographic predictability cannot be confirmed.
problem_solved: It remains unclear how broadly information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race is detectable across organs and disease states in routine histopathology.
method: Analyze 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images spanning 25 organs.
Combine pathology foundation-model representations with multiple-instance learning.
Systematically evaluate 69 organ–demographic combinations involving sex, age group, and self-reported race.
impact: This framework can help practitioners audit demographic information encoded in pathology representations and guide fairness and generalization evaluations. Detectable associations alone would not establish biological causes or demonstrate model bias.
visual_elements: Scale graphic highlighting 1.3 million slides, 257,322 patients, and 25 organs.
Pipeline diagram: whole-slide images → foundation-model representations → multiple-instance learning → demographic assessment.
Organ-by-demographic matrix illustrating the 69 evaluated combinations, without inventing performance values.
Three labeled icons representing sex, age group, and self-reported race.
paper_title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
paper_authors: Shengjia Chen, Ruchika Verma, Kevin Clare, Paula Restrepo, Jannes Jegminat
